kicker: A people-search router, read from source

scenes.headline: How treg picks who finds your lead
scenes.sub: One token, many paid providers, ranked by cost per hit.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Treggy! Here is how this open source Clay rival picks a provider for a people search.

scenes.label: What is new
scenes.text: treg holds no contacts. It ranks every provider that can answer by expected cost per hit, then walks them until one finds the person.
scenes.say: It holds no contacts. It ranks every provider by expected cost per hit, and walks the list until one finds the person.

steps.say: Your agent sends a name and a domain, or a profile link. A contract states that question without naming a vendor.
Each provider's adapter maps it onto its own request. Adapters that cannot take it drop out.
The rest are ranked: your own key first, then providers that use everything you sent, then cost.
Then it calls them in order, and returns the first hit with every attempt and its charge.

scenes.title: The cost term
scenes.text: cost per hit = price x P(billed) / P(hit)

parts.note: the list rate from the catalog
parts.say: Price is the list rate from the catalog.

parts.note: equals P(hit) when a miss is free
parts.say: If a miss is free, the chance of being billed equals the hit rate, and they cancel.
So most finders rank by price alone. One that bills every call gets dearer as its hit rate falls.

items.say: An error tries the next, at most two extra.
A miss walks on, usually free.
A hit stops, with advice to verify first.
A spend cap, one dollar by default, stops a runaway.

steps.say: The film claims eighty-five percent cheaper than Clay, for a hundred correct emails.

steps.note: the run behind it is not published
steps.say: The arithmetic holds, but the run behind it is not published.

scenes.label: 27 people, 20 verified emails, rebuilt from the committed CSV
scenes.say: The smaller receipt checks out: twenty seven people, twenty verified emails, fifty eight cents.

scenes.text: Rank by what a hit really costs, and never let a cheaper, looser answer win.
scenes.say: Copy the router: rank by what a hit really costs, and never let a looser answer win.

recap: Ranked by expected cost per hit
scenes.say: A contract states the question. Ranking by cost per hit. Misses walk on, hits stop.
